newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to fly to three more Chinese cities.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to fly to three more Chinese cities.

text.p: Malaysia has secured landing rights to three new destinations in China and an additional frequency each to Beijing and Guangzhou, Bernama news agency reported on Sunday.

The additional routes, to Shanghai, Shenzen and Xiamen, will increase the destinations to be served by Malaysian airlines in China to five, Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik was quoted by Bernama as saying in Rangoon.
Ling is on a three-day visit to Burma after holding air talks in Beijing.

Ling said the Chinese authorities have approved twice weekly flights to Shanghai and Shenzen with immediate effect, while Malaysia can start operating in Xiamen, also on a twice weekly basis, once China takes up fifth freedom rights from Bangkok to Malaysia.
The additional frequency to Beijing and Guangzhou will take effect in 1998, he said. Malaysia Airlines now operates six times weekly to the two cities.
Ling added that the Cabinet would decide who would operate the new routes and the additional frequency.
"We will discuss with all the national-designated airlines because these are new routes and frequencies," he said.
Apart from Malaysia Airlines, the other national-designated airlines are Air Asia and Saega.
